module_document.title: Bacterial Lol-dependent outer-membrane lipoprotein trafficking
module_document.description: A diderm-bacterial mechanism that extracts mature lipoproteins from the periplasmic leaflet of the inner membrane and delivers them for incorporation into the outer membrane. ATP-coupled release is performed by a LolC1-LolE1-LolD2 or homodimeric LolF2-LolD2 assembly, without translocating cargo across the inner-membrane bilayer. A periplasmic LolA carrier then transfers cargo to a compatible classical or distant LolB-like inserter, while bifunctional carrier/inserter proteins provide an alternative delivery architecture. The machinery and substrate selectivity vary among lineages, and conditional alternative delivery can preserve some lipoprotein localization when known LolA/LolB proteins are absent.

module_document.notes: Boundary excludes upstream Sec/Tat translocation and Lgt/LspA/Lnt maturation, as well as downstream T9 secretion, gliding and surface exposure. Matched full member panels are ECOLI, PSEPK and ACIAD, with different evidence tiers; complete panel does not mean every step or native whole-module flux was directly assayed. FLAJ1 and CB15 are delivery-only exemplars in this member set. Classical TIGR00548 and distant DUF4292 insertion are separate realizers. PTHR35869:SF1 alone does not establish cargo specificity. Membrane units contribute coupled subfunctions to complex-level release; LolD enables ATP hydrolysis. Conditional LolDE reconstitution and stress-dependent LolAB bypass are acknowledged outside the canonical profiles.
